# East-west fabric research

Question: Which checks diagnose east-west fabric quality within a two-hour GB300 rack certification window?

Research date: 2026-10-11.

Audience: rack-bench developers and datacenter operators in Chennai, India.
Target: GB300 NVL72-class rack with 18 trays.
Expected answer: seven evidence briefs, a failure-mode catalog, suite tables, and implementation tickets.
Scope: RDMA rails, NCCL collectives, topology, congestion, routing, failures, SHARP, scale, and telemetry.
Exclusions: north-south internet, storage design, project code changes, and live fabric tests.
Sources: primary technical documents, provider documents, papers, and exact local file evidence.

The map has seven independent evidence branches.
No branch needs another branch's result before research starts.
The distilled report uses all seven branches.
A `done` state means accepted research, not a certified fabric.
Each lesson states its evidence limits.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
N01["Neocloud fabric evidence"]
N02["Hyperscaler fabric runbooks"]
N03["AI lab validation practice"]
N04["Large-company fabric mechanisms"]
N05["ClusterMAX east-west coverage"]
N06["Academic measurement methods"]
N07["Fabric diagnosis reading canon"]
```

| Node | Question | Dependencies | Acceptance condition | Child | State |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| N01 | What fabric evidence can neocloud tenants obtain? | None | Separate measurements, claims, configuration, and missing disclosure. | neoclouds | done |
| N02 | How do hyperscalers verify and diagnose GPU fabrics? | None | Give versioned configuration, verification, and diagnosis evidence. | hyperscalers | done |
| N03 | How do AI labs find communication failures at scale? | None | Connect topology, collective patterns, overlap, and rank delays to checks. | ai-labs | done |
| N04 | Which large-company mechanisms explain fabric failures? | None | Separate production mechanisms, papers, and tenant-visible checks. | large-companies | done |
| N05 | What does current ClusterMAX test and leave untested? | None | Check suite details and separate public audit from private tests. | clustermax | done |
| N06 | Which academic methods diagnose congestion and collective limits? | None | Explain formulas, measurement controls, counter meaning, and limits. | academia | done |
| N07 | Which references best support fabric diagnosis? | None | Rank books and technical documents with tool-specific limits. | books | done |

## N01: Neocloud fabric evidence

What can a tenant measure independently?
This question prevents provider capability claims from becoming PASS evidence.
A rail is a logical communication path. A plane describes physical topology.
Do not assume one rail equals one independent plane.

Nebius publishes 400 Gb/s per GPU NIC and 3.2 Tb/s per eight-GPU VM.
These numbers describe capability, not the Chennai rack's measured throughput.
CoreWeave supplies NCCL recipes and a measured-baseline diagnosis method.
Crusoe supplies topology files. Lambda supplies fabric and link-health descriptions.
The reviewed pages do not supply comparable measured GB300 rail tables.

Run each rail separately, then run all required rails concurrently.
Keep baseline collectives separate from SHARP tests.
SHARP moves reduction work into switches; its presence does not prove actual use.
A NCCL PASS does not prove UCX/NIXL health.
NVL72 traffic can use NVLink across trays, not RDMA.
Check transport logs and traffic-counter changes, or use a cross-rack peer.

Use N02 for transport-specific verification. Use N06 for bandwidth interpretation.
Gap: public evidence does not set target-rack thresholds or continuous flap rates.

Sources: [Nebius fabric](https://docs.nebius.com/compute/clusters/gpu),
[CoreWeave diagnosis](https://docs.coreweave.com/support/sunk/articles/what-do-nccl-errors-mean),
[full brief](neoclouds.md), [accepted node record](nodes/N01.md).

## N02: Hyperscaler fabric runbooks

Which transport does the benchmark actually use?
The answer changes the command, expected logs, and useful counters.
AWS EFA uses `aws-ofi-nccl` and the Libfabric EFA provider.
It does not use the ordinary NCCL verbs `NET/IB` path.
AWS documents `fi_info -p efa -t FI_EP_RDM` and provider-selection logs.
A successful launch alone does not prove GPU-memory RDMA or balanced rails.

Azure ND H100 provides dedicated InfiniBand connections for its eight GPUs.
Google A3 High/Edge uses TCPX. A3 Mega uses TCPXO.
A3 Ultra uses RoCE/MRDMA with gIB.
These stacks need different verification procedures.
Google's network-tier setting does not prove RDMA selection.
Google's GB300 A4X Max uses an 18-instance, 72-GPU NVLink subblock.
RoCE connects different subblocks. An intra-subblock collective can therefore avoid RDMA.

Record the exact SKU, versions, topology, command, environment, and selected plugin.
NCCL 2.21+ normally selects RoCE GIDs dynamically.
ClusterMAX reports a provider-specific forced-GID workaround.
Keep that exception separate from the general default guidance.
Do not force index 3 on every RoCE fabric.

Use N07 for version-matched tool guidance.
Gap: public sources do not give portable switch thresholds or a complete HNDR diagnosis runbook.

Sources: [AWS EFA](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/efa-start-nccl.html),
[Google GPU networking](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus/gpu-network-bandwidth),
[NCCL networking](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting/networking_troubleshooting.html),
[full brief](hyperscalers.md), [accepted node record](nodes/N02.md).

## N03: AI lab validation practice

Does a slow collective prove a network fault?
No. A rank can wait because another rank starts communication late.
A rank is one participating process in the collective.
A straggler is a rank that delays shared progress.

PyTorch shows how late compute or data preparation increases another rank's synchronization time.
Record collective entry, exit, GPU state, and CPU progress.
Compare these timestamps with rail throughput and counter changes.
Do not name a network cause from synchronization time alone.

Meta reports topology and routing effects on collective performance.
DeepSeek documents an eight-plane topology for V3's H800 infrastructure.
That topology does not establish the GB300 rack's topology.
AllReduce, AllGather, and AlltoAll place different demands on the fabric.
Test each pattern across small and large payloads.
Keep standalone collective results separate from compute-overlap results.
Overlap can hide communication time or consume compute resources.

Use N04 for congestion mechanisms. Use N06 for measurement controls.
Gap: public lab reports do not supply validated GB300 thresholds or a tested two-hour schedule.

Sources: [PyTorch stragglers](https://pytorch.org/blog/straggler-mitigation),
[DeepSeek infrastructure](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.09343v1),
[full brief](ai-labs.md), [accepted node record](nodes/N03.md).

## N04: Large-company fabric mechanisms

Why can healthy links produce a slow collective?
Flow placement, routing, queues, and congestion control change shared path capacity.
ECMP distributes flows across equal-cost paths.
Low flow entropy can place many flows on one path.
PFC pauses selected Ethernet priorities. ECN marks congestion for transport response.

Meta reports ECMP collisions and placement-sensitive performance.
Host throughput can show a symptom but cannot prove its switch-side cause.
Request time-correlated queue, route, pause, drop, and link-event evidence.
Without that evidence, state that the cause remains unconfirmed.
An ECN or CNP increase can show a working congestion response.
Do not treat every pause or congestion mark as a failure.

Swift belongs to Google and describes delay-based congestion control.
Jupiter supplies production network-engineering evidence.
Microsoft Sirius supplies prototype and simulation evidence, not production proof.
Keep those evidence classes separate.
Use approved fault tests only outside the default non-destructive bench.

Use N05 to compare published suite coverage. Use N07 for device-specific counter definitions.
Gap: the bounded search does not identify the “self-serving fabric” seed title.

Sources: [Meta RoCE](https://engineering.fb.com/2024/08/05/data-center-engineering/roce-network-distributed-ai-training-at-scale/),
[Google Swift](https://research.google/pubs/swift-delay-is-simple-and-effective-for-congestion-control-in-the-datacenter),
[full brief](large-companies.md), [accepted node record](nodes/N04.md).

## N05: ClusterMAX east-west coverage

Which ClusterMAX checks can the project reproduce?
The public `cmax` tool supplies audit checks, not the private performance suite.
ClusterMAX 3.0 describes collective sweeps from 8 B to 16 GB.
It describes MPI and PyTorch paths, per-rail RDMA, scaling, and endurance tests.
Its eight-hour concurrent GPU/network burn-in exceeds the two-hour bench window.

Prime Intellect's example reaches 13 nodes. Google's example reaches 16 nodes.
Neither example establishes the suite's overall maximum scale.
ClusterMAX disables NVLink in described NVL72 tests to isolate scale-out traffic.
Keep scale-out-isolated results separate from production-layout results.

An Oracle example reaches 391 Gb/s on all eight rails before RDMA teardown fails.
The ports still show ACTIVE at 400 Gb/s.
Check cleanup completion and run a fresh post-test connection canary.
Peak throughput cannot replace that evidence.

The public methodology does not describe link-flap/node-kill injection during collectives.
Do not attribute those tests to ClusterMAX from the project README alone.
Use N06 to check curve interpretation and bandwidth formulas.
Gap: private commands, thresholds, raw results, and several fault-test methods remain undisclosed.

Sources: [ClusterMAX 3.0](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/clustermax-30-the-industry-standard),
[public cmax](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/clustermax),
[full brief](clustermax.md), [accepted node record](nodes/N05.md).

## N06: Academic measurement methods

How can the suite compare different collective results correctly?
`algbw` describes operation throughput. `busbw` applies a collective-specific traffic correction.
Neither value directly counts bytes through the NIC.

For an S-byte ring AllReduce, each rank sends `2S(n−1)/n` bytes across both phases.
Each rank receives the same volume. Here, n is the rank count.
NCCL-tests uses `2(n−1)/n` to correct AllReduce algorithm bandwidth.
Its AllGather and AlltoAll correction uses `(n−1)/n` with their defined payload accounting.
Check the pinned tool's definition before calculation.

Small messages expose fixed latency. Large messages expose throughput limits.
Algorithm and protocol changes can cause valid steps or dips.
Do not require strict bandwidth monotonicity.
Repeat suspect points and keep algorithm/protocol metadata.
Compare isolated rails with concurrent rails and both directions.
Keep host-memory and GPU-memory paths separate.

Use N07 for tool and counter limits.
Gap: the evidence does not supply a matched current GB300 RoCE-versus-InfiniBand comparison.
No universal line-rate percentage follows from these papers.

Sources: [NCCL-tests formulas](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl-tests/blob/master/doc/PERFORMANCE.md),
[DCQCN](https://conferences.sigcomm.org/sigcomm/2015/pdf/papers/p523.pdf),
[full brief](academia.md), [accepted node record](nodes/N06.md).

## N07: Fabric diagnosis reading canon

Which references support reliable diagnosis?
Books explain measurement method. Current tool and device documents define commands and counters.
Gregg's Systems Performance gives utilization, saturation, and error checks.
Jain gives experiment and statistical methods. Kurose and Ross gives network fundamentals.
None replaces a current RDMA or switch manual.
The [eleven-source supplement](oreilly/research.md) adds optional architecture and host context.
Shanley supports native-InfiniBand concepts; Dutt supports optional Ethernet architecture context.
ISBN 020163354X identifies TCP/IP Illustrated Volume 2.
Catalog and TOC evidence does not establish current RDMA procedures or measured PASS.

Use version-matched NCCL, perftest, and fabric-manager documents first.
Match perftest client/server versions and parameters.
Check local GPU-memory support instead of assuming a build supports GB300.
Perftest latency uses half the round-trip time; asymmetric paths can distort that estimate.

Save raw counters, units, widths, timestamps, and reset state.
Historical errors do not prove an error during the test.
Counter units and counter width describe different properties.
InfiniBand data counters use four-octet units.
Base PMA counters saturate; optional extended counters use wider fields.
Check the exported counter type before calculating its change.
Host counters cannot prove every switch queue remains healthy.
`ibdump` has capture limits and an announced move to `mstflint`.
A clean capture does not prove a lossless fabric.

Use all seven lessons in the [distilled suite design](docs/network-bench-research.md).
Gap: deployed firmware, privileges, switch access, and the two-hour execution time remain unknown.

Sources: [Gregg](https://www.brendangregg.com/systems-performance-2nd-edition-book.html),
[perftest](https://github.com/linux-rdma/perftest), [ibdump](https://github.com/Mellanox/ibdump),
[Linux counter ABI](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-class-infiniband),
[full brief](books.md), [accepted node record](nodes/N07.md).

# Network Troubleshooting Tools — Sloan supplement

Research date: 2026-10-11. All claims below carry a source URL.

Superseded draft. Use [the corrected source note](oreilly/troubleshooting-tools.md).
Do not use this draft as accepted evidence.

## 1. Identity and access

**Verified facts.** Joseph D. Sloan, *Network Troubleshooting Tools*, O’Reilly, first edition, August 2001; 364 pages per O’Reilly/Amazon catalog; ISBN 0-596-00186-X / 978-0-596-00186-5. The book itself states “First Edition” and copyright 2001. O’Reilly Learning Library URL supplied for this task returned HTTP 403, so authenticated access was not available; this is an access restriction, not evidence that the book is absent. A publicly accessible scan supplies the title/copyright page and contents. [O’Reilly catalog](https://learning.oreilly.com/library/view/-/059600186X/?orm_source=mcp) · [public full-text scan, title/copyright and TOC](http://www.nylxs.com/docs/networktroubleshootingtools.pdf) · [Amazon catalog details](https://www.amazon.com/Network-Troubleshooting-OReilly-System-Administration/dp/059600186X)

## 2. Verified chapters

The scanned book’s TOC verifies these especially relevant chapters (chapter numbers and titles are observed facts):

- Ch. 1, “Network Management and Troubleshooting” (p. 1).
- Ch. 3, “Connectivity Testing” (p. 45).
- Ch. 4, “Path Characteristics” (p. 71).
- Ch. 5, “Packet Capture” (p. 100).
- Ch. 6, “Device Discovery and Mapping” (p. 134); ch. 7, “Device Monitoring with SNMP” (p. 160).
- Ch. 8, “Performance Measurement Tools” (p. 194); ch. 9, “Testing Connectivity Protocols” (p. 224); ch. 12, “Troubleshooting Strategies” (p. 273).

The book self-describes as a tutorial on information-collection tools and techniques, chiefly freely available Unix tools, mostly Ethernet/TCP/IP. These are not RDMA/NCCL chapters. [Book scan, TOC and preface](http://www.nylxs.com/docs/networktroubleshootingtools.pdf)

## 3. Relevance to the Chennai east-west bench

**Inference.** Its durable contribution is a diagnostic sequence—establish baseline, check connectivity and path, collect packet/device/performance evidence, then combine tools—rather than any current accelerator-fabric procedure. The preface explicitly emphasizes proactive knowledge of normal behavior and information collection; ch. 12 provides troubleshooting strategy. This maps usefully onto an 18-tray, two-hour GB300 NVL72-class bench as a discipline: take before/after evidence, isolate the failing layer, and keep the outcome measured. It does not establish a PASS threshold or substitute for measurements.

For the actual target, prioritize current, domain-specific evidence: NCCL logs and `nccl-tests` for collective goodput, `perftest` for RDMA link/path tests, and deployed vendor/fabric telemetry for rail topology, ECN/PFC and flaps. Compare measured goodput with line rate explicitly; collect counters as deltas and correlate with link/port events. Those are implementation recommendations inferred from the target and modern sources, not techniques asserted by Sloan. [NCCL troubleshooting](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/archives/nccl_2312/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting.html) · [NCCL tests](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl-tests) · [perftest upstream](https://github.com/linux-rdma/perftest) · [ibdiagnet manual](https://docs.nvidia.com/ibdiagnet-infiniband-fabric-diagnostic-tool-user-manual-v2-11.pdf)

## 4. Portable diagnosis techniques (adaptations, not RDMA instrumentation)

1. **Baseline before fault-finding.** Record the normal configuration and observed behavior, then compare the loaded run. Adaptation: save per-rail link state/counters and NCCL/perftest results before and after the two-hour run. Sloan’s proactive-baseline principle is explicit; choosing rail counters and the run window is our inference. [Book scan, ch. 1](http://www.nylxs.com/docs/networktroubleshootingtools.pdf)
2. **Layered connectivity ladder.** Separate local interface/link, peer connectivity, path, and application/collective checks rather than treating one successful ping as proof of service. Adaptation: use ping/route checks only as preliminary reachability evidence, then RDMA tests and NCCL. TCP/IP-era probes do not prove verbs or GPU data-path health. [Book scan, chs. 3–4](http://www.nylxs.com/docs/networktroubleshootingtools.pdf) · [NCCL troubleshooting](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/archives/nccl_2312/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting.html)
3. **Capture and correlate, with restraint.** Use packet capture to investigate a targeted suspected protocol/path issue, and correlate its time with performance symptoms. Adaptation: ordinary TCP/Ethernet captures are not the first-line visibility for RDMA payloads; use them only where the deployed transport and capture point make them meaningful. Prefer NIC/switch counters and fabric tools for ECN/PFC and port events. [Book scan, ch. 5](http://www.nylxs.com/docs/networktroubleshootingtools.pdf) · [ibdiagnet manual](https://docs.nvidia.com/ibdiagnet-infiniband-fabric-diagnostic-tool-user-manual-v2-11.pdf)
4. **Measure at multiple scopes and distinguish capacity from achieved throughput.** Sloan’s contents cover path characteristics and performance measurement. Adaptation: report per-rail/link measurements and collective goodput separately; compare both against line-rate expectations and note test size/topology. A successful small ping or a single-link bandwidth result is not collective PASS evidence. [Book scan, chs. 4 and 8](http://www.nylxs.com/docs/networktroubleshootingtools.pdf) · [NCCL tests](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl-tests) · [perftest upstream](https://github.com/linux-rdma/perftest)
5. **Combine independent clues; localize before changing.** Use the path/device view alongside host and application evidence; avoid attributing every throughput symptom to the network. Adaptation: correlate NCCL rank/rail behavior with link flaps, error counters, ECN/PFC telemetry and matched RDMA tests before declaring PASS/FAIL. This is a synthesis for this bench, not a ready-made Sloan recipe. [Book scan, ch. 12](http://www.nylxs.com/docs/networktroubleshootingtools.pdf) · [NCCL troubleshooting](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/archives/nccl_2312/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting.html)

## 5. Canon and overlap verdict

**Sibling overlap evidence (read-only inspection).** The internet books brief explicitly lists Sloan at `/home/avirus/.herdr/worktrees/rack-bench/research-internet/.lavish/internet-research/books.md`, lines 510–517: it describes the book as a 2001, 364-page title, notes ping/traceroute/netstat/sniffers/tcpdump, and verdicts **SKIP** because ULSAH 5e ch. 13 and man pages cover those tools newer. Its skip list repeats the same rationale at lines 593–594. This exact overlap is the general TCP/IP troubleshooting toolkit, not the present east-west RDMA/NCCL diagnosis. [Sibling brief, lines 510–517 and 593–594](file:///home/avirus/.herdr/worktrees/rack-bench/research-internet/.lavish/internet-research/books.md#L510)

The network canon already names Gregg/Jain/Kurose and modern NCCL/perftest/vendor sources. Sloan adds little to that tool canon: it predates modern RDMA fabrics, GPU collectives, current congestion telemetry and rail-aware diagnosis. The sibling’s SKIP is therefore correct for the internet track, but this narrowly scoped supplemental extraction is useful as a **SKIM** for general diagnostic sequencing—not a canon addition or required reading. Do not re-research or reuse the sibling brief’s north-south suite. [Network canon](books.md) · [NCCL troubleshooting](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/archives/nccl_2312/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting.html) · [perftest](https://github.com/linux-rdma/perftest)

## Gaps

- O’Reilly authenticated catalog access was blocked (HTTP 403); the public scan verified first edition, copyright, and chapter list, and catalog metadata verifies the listed pagination. No claim is made about later editions; the inspected scan is explicitly the first edition. [O’Reilly catalog](https://learning.oreilly.com/library/view/-/059600186X/?orm_source=mcp) · [public scan](http://www.nylxs.com/docs/networktroubleshootingtools.pdf)
- No Sloan material verifies GB300/NVL72 behavior, NCCL release requirements, rail mapping, PFC/ECN thresholds, telemetry access, or two-hour coverage feasibility. Confirm these against the deployed hardware/software manuals and measure them on the bench; PASS remains measured, not vendor-claimed. [NCCL troubleshooting](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/archives/nccl_2312/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting.html) · [NCCL tests](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl-tests) · [perftest](https://github.com/linux-rdma/perftest)
